title: The Longest Word Without a Repeated Letter

concept.title: A set of letters as one number
body: Choose some of the words and glue them together so that **no letter appears twice** in the result. The only thing that matters about a chosen set of words is the **set of letters used**. There are 26 letters, so a set of letters fits in the bits of an integer: bit `c` is 1 if the letter number `c` is used. Two words can be glued only if their masks have **no common bit**: `mask1 & mask2 == 0`.

body.code:
def best(masks, lengths, i, used):
    if i == len(masks):
        return 0
    result = best(masks, lengths, i + 1, used)                 # skip word i
    if masks[i] >= 0 and masks[i] & used == 0:                 # word i fits
        result = max(result, lengths[i] + best(masks, lengths, i + 1, used | masks[i]))
    return result

body: A word that already repeats a letter inside itself can never be used; give it the mask `-1` so that it is always skipped. The recursion makes a take-or-skip decision for every word, so there are `2^n` leaves at most, but a taken word that clashes with the used letters is never explored: a conflict ends that branch at once.

statement: You are given `n` words of lowercase letters. Choose some of the words (possibly none) and write them one after another so that **all the letters of the result are different**. Print the largest possible length of the result.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` words.

examples.note: The words un and iq fit together (u, n, i, q are different), and ue cannot be added because u would repeat. The best length is 4.

hints: Represent the letters of a word as a bit mask; a word with a repeated letter is unusable.
Two words fit together only if their masks share no bit.
For every word decide: skip it, or take it if it fits.

explanation: Each word becomes a bit mask of its letters (or -1 if it repeats a letter). The recursion either skips a word or takes it when its mask does not overlap the letters already used, and returns the best total length.
solution.complexity: Time O(2^n) in the worst case, space O(n).

code.python:
def best(masks, lengths, i, used):
    if i == len(masks):
        return 0
    result = best(masks, lengths, i + 1, used)
    if masks[i] >= 0 and masks[i] & used == 0:
        result = max(result, lengths[i] + best(masks, lengths, i + 1, used | masks[i]))
    return result

n = int(input())
words = input().split()

masks = []
lengths = []
for w in words:
    mask = 0
    for ch in w:
        bit = 1 << (ord(ch) - 97)
        if mask & bit:
            mask = -1
            break
        mask |= bit
    masks.append(mask)
    lengths.append(len(w))
print(best(masks, lengths, 0, 0))
